title: Grateful Dead Live at Onondaga War Memorial  on 1971-10-27
lineage: Bertha Remaster of the Master Reel/Cassette source
source: SBD > MR > CASS > DAT > DAW(Bertha) > Audio DVD > DVD Audio Extractor v.3.3.2 (audio files extracted prior to burning to DVD disc) > 24/48 wav > downsampled to 44.1 wav with Wave Lab v.5.00a > dithered from 24 to 16 bit depth with Wave Lab UV22 HR Plugin > SBEs fixed with shntool v.2.0.3 (by set) > FLAC encoding with FLAC Frontend v.1.7.1 Etree Edition, FLAC v.1.1.2 (level 8)

ai_review.summary: Excellent pre‑FM soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1971 show, highlighted by a fiery Bertha and a soaring Comes A Time.
ai_review.review: The recording is a superbly remastered WAER soundboard tape that presents the band’s raw, metallic rock energy with crystal‑clear instrument separation – Jerry, Phil and Bob are front‑and‑center while Keith’s keys sit perfectly in the pocket.  The performance itself is spirited, featuring standout moments such as Comes A Time, RR Blues, Cumberland Blues, One More Saturday Night and Bertha, all delivered with tight breaks that keep the momentum flowing.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both musical performance (standout songs, energetic playing) and audio quality (clear, well‑balanced remaster), with only one neutral star rating lacking commentary.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered WAER tape; crisp, clear mix with prominent guitars, vocals and Keith's keyboards. No notable drop‑outs or muffiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: High‑octane, almost angry performance with solid breaks between songs; the set moves smoothly through new 1972 repertoire while maintaining classic Grateful Dead momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Prominent in the mix; passionate vocals with a touch of falsetto on Comes A Time.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is prominent and well‑balanced in the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Guitar and vocal presence highlighted throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboards are right in the pocket and surprisingly clear for his early tenure.
